bull.b: Scale-driven margin expansion reflects durable unit economics: high gross margins plus expanded EBIT margin show pricing power and operating leverage from recurring sensor volumes. Sustained margins support reinvestment in R&D, commercialization and long-term free cash flow generation.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and improved leverage
bull.b: Robust cash conversion and materially lower leverage provide durable financial flexibility to fund manufacturing scale-up, clinical programs, M&A and buybacks. A stronger balance sheet reduces refinancing risk and cushions timing mismatches with reimbursement milestones.

bull.t: Recurring consumable model & payer coverage momentum
bull.b: CGM consumables create repeatable, subscription-like revenue. Expanded PBM coverage and higher-device conversion deepen penetration in large commercial pools, raising lifetime revenue per user and lowering reliance on constant new-customer acquisition over the medium term.

bear.b: A sustained slowdown in top-line growth risks undermining the leverage inherent in high-margin consumables: slower unit adoption or penetration can make it harder to meet long-range revenue targets and compress future operating margin and FCF expansion assumptions.

CMS coverage is a structural demand inflection for non-insulin type 2 lives; timing or restrictive coverage conditions could materially delay or reduce uptake across government beneficiaries, weakening projected addressable market growth and near-to-medium term reimbursement-driven volumes.

bear.t: Operational execution and quality risk from manufacturing ramp
bear.b: Historical quality issues and the Ireland production ramp create persistent operational risk: manufacturing scale-up can raise scrap, warranty and training costs and impair customer experience. Sustained execution lapses would erode NPS, increase costs, and slow adoption despite favorable clinical evidence.
